Published Definition: A uniquely identifiable real-world object, event, or concept about which data is stored. Entities are described by attributes and may have relationships with other entities.
Name: entity

Original Definition: Core, non-transactional data that describes key business entities (e.g., persons in BC, services, assets, locations). Master Data should represent Authoritative Data so it can be trusted and used with confidence by the entire organization.
Published Definition: Core, non-transactional data that describes key business entities (e.g., persons in BC, services, assets, locations). Master Data should represent Authoritative Data so it can be trusted and used with confidence by the entire organization.
Name: master-data

Original Definition: Data that is used to describe or classify other data (e.g., lists of disease types, gender codes, building materials, etc.)
Published Definition: Data that is used to describe or classify other data (e.g., lists of disease types, gender codes, building materials, etc.)
Name: reference-data

Original Definition: A system that consolidates and harmonizes data from multiple systems of record to provide a trusted reference for sharing data.
Published Definition: A system that consolidates and harmonizes data from multiple systems of record to provide a trusted reference for sharing data.
Name: system-of-reference

Original Definition: Accuracy measures the degree to which data describes the real-world phenomena it is intended to represent.
Published Definition: Accuracy measures the degree to which data describes the real-world phenomena it is intended to represent.
Name: accuracy

Original Definition: The proportion of stored data against the definition of “100% complete”. Completeness is contextual to the purpose for data collection (for example, is the scope of collection the whole province or a region?)
Published Definition: The proportion of stored data against the definition of “100% complete”. Completeness is contextual to the purpose for data collection (for example, is the scope of collection the whole province or a region?)
Name: completeness

Original Definition: Data Quality Assessment Framework defines standardized dimensions of data quality and associated measures for assessing the level of data quality. A measure may apply at the dataset, record, and/or attribute level.
Published Definition: Data Quality Assessment Framework defines standardized dimensions of data quality and associated measures for assessing the level of data quality. A measure may apply at the dataset, record, and/or attribute level.
Name: data-quality-assessment-framework

Original Definition: A Data Quality Scorecard is an instance or snapshot of a dataset’s data quality measures, as defined by the Data Quality Assessment Framework.
Published Definition: A Data Quality Scorecard is an instance or snapshot of a dataset’s data quality measures, as defined by the Data Quality Assessment Framework.
Name: data-quality-scorecard

Original Definition: The degree to which data represent reality from the required point in time. Includes currency (are the data up to date?) and latency (when was the data last updated?)
Published Definition: The degree to which data represent reality from the required point in time. Includes currency (are the data up to date?) and latency (when was the data last updated?)
Name: timeliness

Original Definition: The degree to which there are no duplicate data.
Published Definition: The degree to which there are no duplicate data.
Name: uniqueness

Original Definition: The degree to which data conforms to its defined domain of values, including the rules for allowed formats, structures, acceptable ranges, and lists of permissible values.
Published Definition: The degree to which data conforms to its defined domain of values, including the rules for allowed formats, structures, acceptable ranges, and lists of permissible values.
Name: validity

Original Definition: Consent is a voluntary agreement by an individual for their personal information to be accessed, verified or used by a government service for specified purposes such as determining or verifying eligibility for other benefits or services.
Published Definition: Consent is a voluntary agreement by an individual for their personal information to be accessed, verified or used by a government service for specified purposes such as determining or verifying eligibility for other benefits or services.
Name: consent

Original Definition:
Delegation is a secure, formalized process that permits an individual to authorize another individual to access, manage or act on their behalf within digital government services.  
Delegation enables individuals —especially the elderly, persons with disabilities, or those with limited digital literacy—to benefit from digital services without being excluded.
Published Definition:
Delegation is a secure, formalized process that permits an individual to authorize another individual to access, manage or act on their behalf within digital government services.  
Delegation enables individuals —especially the elderly, persons with disabilities, or those with limited digital literacy—to benefit from digital services without being excluded.
Name: delegation

Original Definition: SDX as a capability/piece of functionality is the ability to move data securely and lawfully between parties. Includes technical patterns, governance, tooling and audit controls.
Published Definition: SDX as a capability/piece of functionality is the ability to move data securely and lawfully between parties. Includes technical patterns, governance, tooling and audit controls.
Name: secure-data-exchange-sdx

Original Definition: The ability for multiple systems to reliably exchange and understand data using standardized machine-readable formats, shared semantic definitions, and common technical protocols in alignment with applicable policies and standards.
Name: data-interoperability

Original Definition: A government service is a way for people to give or get something they need. An example is registering a child’s birth or incorporating a business.
Name: government-service

Original Definition:
Unmarried couples are considered spouses if they meet either of the following criteria:
1) demonstrate qualities consistent with a marriage-like relationship while residing together for 12 consecutive months, or
2) if they declare that they are in a marriage-like relationship.
Married couples who can demonstrate they have separated are exempted from being considered spouses. 
Separated means that they have legally separated, in divorce 
proceedings, severed financial interdependence or social and familial interdependence, etc.
Published Definition:
Unmarried couples are considered spouses if they meet either of the following criteria:
1) demonstrate qualities consistent with a marriage-like relationship while residing together for 12 consecutive months, or
2) if they declare that they are in a marriage-like relationship.
Married couples who can demonstrate they have separated are exempted from being considered spouses. 
Separated means that they have legally separated, in divorce 
proceedings, severed financial interdependence or social and familial interdependence, etc.
Name: spouse

Original Definition:
Primary Documented Surname from the BCSC.
The individual's documented surname recorded from valid identification.
Published Definition: The individual's documented surname recorded from valid identification.
Name: surname

Original Definition:
Primary Documented Given Name from the BCSC.
The individual's documented given name recorded from valid identification.
Note: This returns first name only and may not include all portions of the first name.
Published Definition: The individual's documented given name recorded from valid identification.
Name: given-name

Original Definition:
Birth Date from the BCSC.
The individual's documented birth date recorded from valid identification.
Name: birth-date

Original Definition:
Sex from the BCSC.	
The individual's documented sex recorded from valid identification.
Name: sex

Original Definition:
Residential address from the BCSC.
The street address lines of an individual's provided residential address.
Name: street-address

Original Definition: The city, municipality or district of an individual's provided residential address.
Name: locality

Original Definition: The two-letter province code of an individual's provided residential address.
Name: province

Original Definition: The postal code of the individual's provided residential address.
Name: postal-code

Original Definition: The two-letter country code of an individual's provided residential address.
Name: country

Original Definition: The email address provided by an individual that has been verified with email delivery once (Personal or Business).
Name: verified-email

Original Definition: Dependents include a spouse, children and dependent post-secondary students.
Published Definition: Dependents include a spouse, children and dependent post-secondary students.
Name: dependents

Original Definition:
In relation to another person, it means anyone who resides with the person and who is the spouse of the other person, or is a dependent child of the person, or indicates a parental role for the person's dependent child. 
Note: Adults are not considered to be dependants of each other on the sole basis of demonstrating a parental role towards the same child.

Dependant in the SDPR context refers to a child who lives with the applicant more than 50% of the time
Published Definition: In relation to another person, it means anyone who resides with the person and who is the spouse of the other person, or is a dependent child of the person, or indicates a parental role for the person's dependent child.  Note: Adults are not considered to be dependants of each other on the sole basis of demonstrating a parental role towards the same child.
Name: dependant

Published Definition: With respect to a parent, it means a child, other than a child who is 18 years of age and is a person with disabilities, who resides in the parent's place of residence for more than 50 per cent of each month and relies on that parent for the necessities of life.   In relation to a dependent child, a parent includes but is not limited to: A biological mother or father;  An adoptive mother or father;  A person with legal custody, other than a director under the Child, Family and Community Service Act or an administrator under the Adoption Act;  A person with legal guardianship, other than a director under the Child, Family and Community Service Act or an administrator under the Adoption Act OR  A person who is the parent of the parenting dependent child.A client temporarily caring for a child without legal custody or guardianship may also be considered a parent. Caring for a child may include one or more of the following, but is not limited to:making day-to-day decisions affecting the child;having day-to-day care, control and supervision of the child;making decisions respecting where the child will reside;making decisions respecting the child's education and participation in extracurricular activities;making decisions respecting the child's cultural, linguistic, religious and spiritual upbringing and heritage;applying for a passport, licence, permit, benefit, privilege or other thing for the child;exercising any other responsibilities reasonably necessary to nurture the child's development. Note: Under certain circumstance a dependent child may be excluded from a family unit. For example, when two parents are separated but are residing together and the dependent child resides with both the separated parents 100% of the time.
Name: dependent-child

Original Definition: Each B.C. resident enrolled with the Medical Services Plan (MSP) is given a unique lifetime identifier for health care called a Personal Health Number (PHN). Your PHN remains the same, regardless of any changes to personal status, and can be found on your BC Services Card.
Published Definition: Each B.C. resident enrolled with the Medical Services Plan (MSP) is given a unique lifetime identifier for health care called a Personal Health Number (PHN). Your PHN remains the same, regardless of any changes to personal status, and can be found on your BC Services Card.
Comments: This definition needs improvement as it is not currently worded as a definition.
Name: personal-health-number

Original Definition: The B.C. Public Service is divided into ministries. Each ministry is responsible for a specific area of public policy, government function or service delivery.
Published Definition: The B.C. Public Service is divided into ministries. Each ministry is responsible for a specific area of public policy, government function or service delivery.
Name: ministries

Original Definition: There are many independent or partially independent agencies, boards and commissions that are essential to effectively governing the province. Agencies include authorities, boards, commissions, corporations and councils. A public agency also includes any bodies established by the government on an interim basis to perform arbitration, regulation or similar functions.
Published Definition: There are many independent or partially independent agencies, boards and commissions that are essential to effectively governing the province. Agencies include authorities, boards, commissions, corporations and councils. A public agency also includes any bodies established by the government on an interim basis to perform arbitration, regulation or similar functions.
Name: central-government-agencies

Original Definition: Crown corporations are owned by the government, but operate at arm’s length from the public service and elected officials.
Published Definition: Crown corporations are owned by the government, but operate at arm’s length from the public service and elected officials.
Name: crown-corporations

Original Definition: Independent boards, commissions and tribunals are established by the government to perform arbitration, regulation or similar functions. The provincial government appoints at least one representative to these agencies.
Published Definition: Independent boards, commissions and tribunals are established by the government to perform arbitration, regulation or similar functions. The provincial government appoints at least one representative to these agencies.
Comments: Need to separate these terms into their own rows.
Name: independent-boards-commissions-and-tribunals

Original Definition: Professional regulatory authorities are government agencies or public organizations with authority delegated by law from the government. They provide oversight and certification to specified regulated occupations in B.C.
Published Definition: Professional regulatory authorities are government agencies or public organizations with authority delegated by law from the government. They provide oversight and certification to specified regulated occupations in B.C.
Name: professional-regulatory-authorities

Published Definition: A government-related organization or agency funded to deliver public services to citizens.  For example, a government ministry, central government agency, Crown corporation, or regulator.
Name: public-body

Original Definition: It is the category of the public body as defined in public bodies defintion.
Published Definition: The category of the public body defined in public bodies definition.
Name: public-body-type

Original Definition:
Residency or "Ordinarily resident" in B.C. refers to the place where the applicant or recipient normally lives the regular routine of their day-to-day life. Indicators may include but are not limited to:•An established “place of residence” in B.C. Learn more by reviewing the support, shelter and special care page
•Residence of spouse, children, and other dependent family members in B.C.
•Legal and other documents indicating B.C. residence, such as utility bills
•B.C. driver's license or BC services card
•Registration of vehicles in B.C.
•Employment or business relationships in B.C.
•Links to community in B.C. through religious organizations, recreational and social clubs, unions, and professional organizations
•Life or health insurance policies in B.C., such as BC Medical Services Plan coverage
•Filing income tax returns as a B.C. resident
•Bank or other financial accounts with a home branch in B.C.
•Applying for government assistance, programs, and/or financial benefits in B.C.
•The frequency, length, purpose, and intention of stays within and outside of B.C.
Repeated instances of leaving BC, returning briefly, and then leaving again would most likely not be considered as ordinarily resident of B.C..
Published Definition:
Residency or "Ordinarily resident" in B.C. refers to the place where the applicant or recipient normally lives the regular routine of their day-to-day life. Indicators may include but are not limited to:

•An established “place of residence” in B.C. Learn more by reviewing the support, shelter and special care page
•Residence of spouse, children, and other dependent family members in B.C.
•Legal and other documents indicating B.C. residence, such as utility bills
•B.C. driver's license or BC services card
•Registration of vehicles in B.C.
•Employment or business relationships in B.C.
•Links to community in B.C. through religious organizations, recreational and social clubs, unions, and professional organizations
•Life or health insurance policies in B.C., such as BC Medical Services Plan coverage
•Filing income tax returns as a B.C. resident
•Bank or other financial accounts with a home branch in B.C.
•Applying for government assistance, programs, and/or financial benefits in B.C.
•The frequency, length, purpose, and intention of stays within and outside of B.C.
Repeated instances of leaving BC, returning briefly, and then leaving again would most likely not be considered as ordinarily resident of B.C..
Name: residency

Original Definition: (a) The person named on a land title form as the person acquiring an interest in land. (b) The person named as applicant in the application section is the person with whom land title staff is authorized to communicate with regarding an application.
Published Definition: (a) The person named on a land title form as the person acquiring an interest in land. (b) The person named as applicant in the application section is the person with whom land title staff is authorized to communicate with regarding an application.
Name: applicant

Original Definition: A transfer of an estate or interest in land (other than by will) to a new owner through sale, lease, or other means. A transfer of title is the conveyance of an estate or interest in land in exchange for some financial consideration, typically a sale.
Published Definition: A transfer of an estate or interest in land (other than by will) to a new owner through sale, lease, or other means. A transfer of title is the conveyance of an estate or interest in land in exchange for some financial consideration, typically a sale.
Name: conveyance

Original Definition: A corporation means a company, a body corporate, a body politic and corporate, an incorporated association or a society, however and wherever incorporated, but does not include a municipality or a corporation sole.
Published Definition: A corporation means a company, a body corporate, a body politic and corporate, an incorporated association or a society, however and wherever incorporated, but does not include a municipality or a corporation sole.
Name: corporation

Original Definition: Land owned and administered by a government, either federal or provincial. In British Columbia, Federal (Canadian) Crown land includes National Parks, Indian Reserves, federal ports and military bases. Provincial Crown land includes provincial parks and all ungranted land (wilderness) within the provincial boundaries. Most of British Columbia is Crown land.
Published Definition: Land owned and administered by a government, either federal or provincial. In British Columbia, Federal (Canadian) Crown land includes National Parks, Indian Reserves, federal ports and military bases. Provincial Crown land includes provincial parks and all ungranted land (wilderness) within the provincial boundaries. Most of British Columbia is Crown land.
Name: crown-land

Original Definition: A document refers to any of the land title forms or supporting material (including survey plans) which are submitted as part of an application to register an interest in land within British Columbia. Examples include: title transfers, mortgages and easements.
Published Definition: A document refers to any of the land title forms or supporting material (including survey plans) which are submitted as part of an application to register an interest in land within British Columbia. Examples include: title transfers, mortgages and easements.
Name: document

Original Definition: Equity is defined as the value of a piece of property (such as a house) after any debts that remain to be paid for it (such as the amount of a mortgage) have been subtracted.
Published Definition: Equity is defined as the value of a piece of property (such as a house) after any debts that remain to be paid for it (such as the amount of a mortgage) have been subtracted.
Name: equity

Original Definition: Fee Simple is the form of ownership of real property (real estate) in which the owner has the right to control and transfer the property at will.
Published Definition: Fee Simple is the form of ownership of real property (real estate) in which the owner has the right to control and transfer the property at will.
Name: fee-simple

Original Definition: A beneficial owner of a relevant trust, a corporate interest holder of a relevant corporation, or a partnership interest holder of a relevant partnership
Published Definition: A beneficial owner of a relevant trust, a corporate interest holder of a relevant corporation, or a partnership interest holder of a relevant partnership
Name: interest-holder
interest-in-land

Original Definition: An enactment that provides the statutory framework for the administration of Crown land, establishes the responsibilities of government Ministers regarding the administration of Crown land and provides for the delegation of certain authorities. Many powers have been delegated to the Surveyor General with respect to Crown land definition and disposition.
Published Definition: An enactment that provides the statutory framework for the administration of Crown land, establishes the responsibilities of government Ministers regarding the administration of Crown land and provides for the delegation of certain authorities. Many powers have been delegated to the Surveyor General with respect to Crown land definition and disposition.
Name: land-act

Original Definition: The Land Owner Transparency Act was passed by the government of British Columbia in May 2019. The first-of-its-kind in Canada, it created an accessible registry of beneficial interests in land in B.C. – the Land Owner Transparency Registry.
Published Definition: The Land Owner Transparency Act was passed by the government of British Columbia in May 2019. The first-of-its-kind in Canada, it created an accessible registry of beneficial interests in land in B.C. – the Land Owner Transparency Registry.
Name: land-owner-transparency-act

Original Definition: A publicly searchable registry of information about beneficial ownership of land in British Columbia. Beneficial owners are people who own or control land indirectly, such as through a corporation, partnership, or trust. The registry is intended to end hidden ownership of land in BC. The Land Owner Transparency Registry launched November 30, 2020, and opened to public search on April 30, 2021.
Published Definition: A publicly searchable registry of information about beneficial ownership of land in British Columbia. Beneficial owners are people who own or control land indirectly, such as through a corporation, partnership, or trust. The registry is intended to end hidden ownership of land in BC. The Land Owner Transparency Registry launched November 30, 2020, and opened to public search on April 30, 2021.
Name: land-owner-transparency-registry

Original Definition:
A comprehensive 400-section statute that prescribes the legal program under which the land title system operates, the Land Title Act designates:
•	The Director of Land Titles to regulate land title practice.
•	The Registrar(s) of Land Titles as the primary statutory decision maker(s) in the administration of the land title system.
The Land Title Act establishes the land title register and requirements respecting its operation and records.
Published Definition:
A comprehensive 400-section statute that prescribes the legal program under which the land title system operates, the Land Title Act designates:
•	The Director of Land Titles to regulate land title practice.
•	The Registrar(s) of Land Titles as the primary statutory decision maker(s) in the administration of the land title system.
The Land Title Act establishes the land title register and requirements respecting its operation and records.
Name: land-title-act

Original Definition: That part of the records of the land title office, including electronic records, where information respecting registered indefeasible titles is stored. It is independently maintained by the LTSA under the statutory authority of the registrars of land titles and in accordance with the requirements of the Land Title Act respecting permanent records retention.
Published Definition: That part of the records of the land title office, including electronic records, where information respecting registered indefeasible titles is stored. It is independently maintained by the LTSA under the statutory authority of the registrars of land titles and in accordance with the requirements of the Land Title Act respecting permanent records retention.
Name: land-title-register

Original Definition: A unique identifier for each parcel of land in the province. It is a text description that may include lot number, plan number, survey system identifiers (Range, Block, Township, District Lot, District, etc.) and other text.
Published Definition: A unique identifier for each parcel of land in the province. It is a text description that may include lot number, plan number, survey system identifiers (Range, Block, Township, District Lot, District, etc.) and other text.
Name: legal-description

Original Definition: Information recorded against a title to land following the receipt of an application concerning matters other than ownership of interests in land, such as statutory restrictions on use (such as the application of a heritage designation bylaw) or rights relating to other land (such as the existence of an appurtenant easement on the title of adjacent land).
Published Definition: Information recorded against a title to land following the receipt of an application concerning matters other than ownership of interests in land, such as statutory restrictions on use (such as the application of a heritage designation bylaw) or rights relating to other land (such as the existence of an appurtenant easement on the title of adjacent land).
Name: legal-notations

Original Definition: An interest in land claimed to secure the payment of a debt or the performance of some other obligation. Examples include Claim of Builders Lien for payment of debt related to labour or materials, Certificate of Lien for payment of strata fees, or Tax Act Liens for payment of various taxes.
Published Definition: An interest in land claimed to secure the payment of a debt or the performance of some other obligation. Examples include Claim of Builders Lien for payment of debt related to labour or materials, Certificate of Lien for payment of strata fees, or Tax Act Liens for payment of various taxes.
Name: lien

Original Definition: An interest in land granted by the registered owner (the mortgagor) to a lender (the mortgagee) as security for a debt.
Published Definition: An interest in land granted by the registered owner (the mortgagor) to a lender (the mortgagee) as security for a debt.
Name: mortgage

Original Definition: A lot, block or other area in which land is held or into which land is subdivided.
Published Definition: A lot, block or other area in which land is held or into which land is subdivided.
Name: parcel

Original Definition: A nine-digit number that uniquely identifies a parcel in the land title register of British Columbia. The registrar assigns PID numbers to parcels for which a title is being entered in the computer register as a registered title. The Land Title Act refers to the PID as the permanent parcel identifier.
Published Definition: A nine-digit number that uniquely identifies a parcel in the land title register of British Columbia. The registrar assigns PID numbers to parcels for which a title is being entered in the computer register as a registered title. The Land Title Act refers to the PID as the permanent parcel identifier.
Name: parcel-identifier-pid

Original Definition: A tax paid when one purchases or gains an interest in property that is registered at the land title office. The provincial Ministry of Finance is responsible for administering the Property Transfer Tax (PTT).
Published Definition: A tax paid when one purchases or gains an interest in property that is registered at the land title office. The provincial Ministry of Finance is responsible for administering the Property Transfer Tax (PTT).
Name: property-transfer-tax

Original Definition: A registered owner is the person who owns an interest in land, either in terms of ownership of title in fee simple, or ownership of a charge. A registered owner is recorded in the land title register upon registration.
Published Definition: A registered owner is the person who owns an interest in land, either in terms of ownership of title in fee simple, or ownership of a charge. A registered owner is recorded in the land title register upon registration.
Name: registered-owner

Original Definition: An official keeper or recorder of records. The Registrar is a statutory decision maker under the Land Title Act, and an employee of the LTSA with a statutory responsibility under LOTA to refuse an application to register an interest in land if the transferee fails to submit a transparency declaration with the application and, in the event the transferee is a reporting body fails to submit a transparency report.
Published Definition: An official keeper or recorder of records. The Registrar is a statutory decision maker under the Land Title Act, and an employee of the LTSA with a statutory responsibility under LOTA to refuse an application to register an interest in land if the transferee fails to submit a transparency declaration with the application and, in the event the transferee is a reporting body fails to submit a transparency report.
Name: registrar

Original Definition: The unique serial number assigned to each entry in the Land Title Register.
Published Definition: The unique serial number assigned to each entry in the Land Title Register.
Name: registration-number

Original Definition: Depending on the context in which it is used title means, on the one hand the right of ownership of land and, on the other, the instruments or evidence of such right. In the register, title to land evidences fee simple ownership of land in one or more Registered Owner(s). Also referred to as land title and indefeasible title. A title may also refer to the ownership of interests in land less than fee simple, such as a mortgage or easement.
Published Definition: Depending on the context in which it is used title means, on the one hand the right of ownership of land and, on the other, the instruments or evidence of such right. In the register, title to land evidences fee simple ownership of land in one or more Registered Owner(s). Also referred to as land title and indefeasible title. A title may also refer to the ownership of interests in land less than fee simple, such as a mortgage or easement.
Name: title

Original Definition: A record issued by the land title office setting out the particulars of a title to land generated from information contained in the register at a specific point in time.
Published Definition: A record issued by the land title office setting out the particulars of a title to land generated from information contained in the register at a specific point in time.
Name: title-search

Original Definition: The voluntary act of a registered owner of an interest in land transferring that interest to another person, typically as a consequence of a sale or gift of the land to that person. The term includes a conveyance, a grant and an assignment.
Published Definition: The voluntary act of a registered owner of an interest in land transferring that interest to another person, typically as a consequence of a sale or gift of the land to that person. The term includes a conveyance, a grant and an assignment.
Name: transfer

Original Definition: An individual or corporation to whom an interest in land is transferred. Includes a grantee, an assignee and a person entitled by transmission to be a registered owner of an interest in land.
Published Definition: An individual or corporation to whom an interest in land is transferred. Includes a grantee, an assignee and a person entitled by transmission to be a registered owner of an interest in land.
Name: transferee

Original Definition: An individual or corporation transferring an interest in land to another party.
Published Definition: An individual or corporation transferring an interest in land to another party.
Name: transferor

Original Definition: A change of ownership of land consequent on death, sale under execution, order of court or other act of law, or on any testamentary settlement or legal succession in the case of intestacy.
Published Definition: A change of ownership of land consequent on death, sale under execution, order of court or other act of law, or on any testamentary settlement or legal succession in the case of intestacy.
Name: transmission

Original Definition: A declaration that is filed by each transferee together with an application to register an interest in land, stating whether the transferee is a reporting body, and, if the transferee is a reporting body, whether the reporting body is a relevant corporation, a trustee or a relevant trust, or a partner of a relevant partnership. Transparency declarations may also be filed at any time, independently of an application to register an interest in land to correct information contained in a previously filed transparency declaration.
Published Definition: A declaration that is filed by each transferee together with an application to register an interest in land, stating whether the transferee is a reporting body, and, if the transferee is a reporting body, whether the reporting body is a relevant corporation, a trustee or a relevant trust, or a partner of a relevant partnership. Transparency declarations may also be filed at any time, independently of an application to register an interest in land to correct information contained in a previously filed transparency declaration.
Name: transparency-declaration

Original Definition: A report that is filed with a transparency declaration on an application to register an interest in land, if the transferee is a reporting body. The transparency report contains information about the reporting body and its interest holder(s).
Published Definition: A report that is filed with a transparency declaration on an application to register an interest in land, if the transferee is a reporting body. The transparency report contains information about the reporting body and its interest holder(s).
Name: transparency-report

Original Definition: A resident of B.C. who is married to or is living and cohabiting in a marriage-like relationship with the applicant.
Published Definition: A resident of B.C. who is married to or is living and cohabiting in a marriage-like relationship with the applicant.
Name: spouse

Original Definition: A resident of B.C. who meets all of the following conditions:Is a child of a beneficiary or a person who stands in place of a parentWho is a minorDoes not have a spouseIs supported by the beneficiary
Published Definition: A resident of B.C. who meets all of the following conditions:Is a child of a beneficiary or a person who stands in place of a parentWho is a minorDoes not have a spouseIs supported by the beneficiary
Name: child

Original Definition: A resident of B.C. who meets all of the following conditions:Older than 18 and younger than 25 years of age In full-time attendance at a recognized post-secondary institution (this includes trade, technical or high schools) Supported by a beneficiary who is the person’s parent or who stands in place of the person’s parent
Published Definition:
A resident of B.C. who meets all of the following conditions:

Older than 18 and younger than 25 years of age

In full-time attendance at a recognized post-secondary institution (this includes trade, technical or high schools)

Supported by a beneficiary who is the person’s parent or who stands in place of the person’s parent
Name: dependent-post-secondary-student

Original Definition: A resident is a person who meets all of the following conditions:A citizen of Canada or lawfully admitted to Canada for permanent residenceMakes their home in B.C.Physically present in B.C. at least six months in a calendar yearEligible B.C. residents (citizens of Canada or persons who are lawfully admitted to Canada for permanent residence) who are outside B.C. for vacation purposes only, are allowed a total absence of up to seven months in a calendar year
Published Definition:
A resident is a person who meets all of the following conditions:

A citizen of Canada or lawfully admitted to Canada for permanent residence

Makes their home in B.C.

Physically present in B.C. at least six months in a calendar year

Eligible B.C. residents (citizens of Canada or persons who are lawfully admitted to Canada for permanent residence) who are outside B.C. for vacation purposes only, are allowed a total absence of up to seven months in a calendar year
Name: resident

Original Definition: A data exchange model/pattern where trusted participants exchange data directly through mutually governed intermediaries.
Name: peer-to-peer-data-exchange
